correctness.rationale: For every nonedge \(uv\), the hypotheses give a unique common neighbor \(w\). The face \(V\setminus\{u,v,w\}\) is codimension one in the \(\Delta_2\)-facet \(V\setminus\{u,v\}\) and is contained in no other \(\Delta_2\)-facet because \(uw\) and \(vw\) are edges. These free faces are distinct. A face surviving all such collapse pairs lies in \(\Delta_3\): if its complement contains at least four vertices, add a vertex different from \(u,v,w\) to obtain a disconnected triple; if the complement has three vertices, the only connected possibility is exactly \(\{u,v,w\}\), whose complementary face was removed. The reverse inclusion \(\Delta_3\subseteq\Delta_2\) is immediate from a nonedge in every disconnected triple. The finite verifier exhausts all qualifying labeled graphs on five and six vertices and separately reconstructs Petersen; its direct Morse check leaves one critical \(0\)-cell and six critical \(6\)-cells.

value.rationale: The collapse is a structural simple-homotopy statement for a natural graph class characterized by unique common neighbors of nonedges. It transports a published connected-triangle-free \(\Delta_2\) theorem to an ordinary \(\Delta_3\) theorem without a new large computation, and immediately evaluates canonical diameter-two, girth-five examples such as Petersen. The exact free-face mechanism also isolates the obstruction created by multiple common neighbors.
